title: IDOR exposes another user's order details on `api.shop-lab.test`
cvss: CVSS:4.0 base 7.1 (network, low complexity, low privileges, high confidentiality)
summary: Order objects are fetched by a sequential ID without verifying the authenticated owner.
precond: Two authorized test accounts (A and B) in the program's lab environment.
steps: 1. Log in as account A and GET /api/orders/1042 (A's own order). 2. Note the response. 3. Using A's token, GET /api/orders/1043 (B's order, ID obtained from B's own account). 4. Observe B's order details returned.
poc: GET /api/orders/1043 with Authorization: Bearer <A-token> returns B's order JSON.
impact: Any authenticated user can read other users' order data (names, addresses, totals) by incrementing an ID.
remediation: Enforce object-level authorization: SELECT ... WHERE id=? AND owner_id=current_user; use centralized policy checks.
triage: Valid. Distinct accounts used; no real user data accessed.
disclaimer: Synthetic training scenario authored for the encyclopedia. Not a real disclosure or a real target.

title: Stored XSS in product review field
cvss: CVSS:4.0 base 6.9 (requires user interaction, changed scope)
summary: Review content is rendered as HTML without sanitization or output encoding.
precond: An authorized test account; a second account to view the review.
steps: 1. As account A, submit a review containing a harmless marker tag. 2. Log in as account B and view the product page. 3. Observe the marker rendered as executable HTML.
poc: Review body: `` executes for viewers.
impact: Script runs in victims' session context; could enable session/token theft or account actions depending on cookie flags.
remediation: Sanitize rich text with an allow-list sanitizer, apply context-aware output encoding, set a strict CSP and HttpOnly cookies.
triage: Valid. Harmless proof; impact explained.

title: Password reset token lacks expiry and rate limiting
summary: Password-reset tokens remain valid indefinitely and no rate limit restricts guessing.
precond: An authorized test account.
steps: 1. Request two password resets for account A. 2. Observe tokens are short and do not expire after use. 3. In the lab, demonstrate that repeated guesses are not throttled.
poc: POST /reset with token values from a controlled sequence; all remain accepted.
impact: An attacker could brute-force a reset token and take over an account.
remediation: Use high-entropy tokens, single-use semantics, short expiry, and rate limiting.
triage: Valid. Medium severity reflecting practical guessing constraints.
